title: Gingerbread Cookie Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Brown sugar, crushed gingerbread biscuits cooked into the base and strained, a pinch of black pepper and biscuit pieces layered in.
summary: Our classic custard, made with brown sugar and crushed gingerbread biscuits cooked into the base and strained out, then a pinch of black pepper and biscuit pieces folded through. Like a frozen gingerbread biscuit.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
gingernut or gingerbread biscuits, finely crushed

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Whisk the brown sugar, yolks and salt in the saucepan, then whisk in the crushed biscuits, cream and milk.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Warm over medium-low heat for a few minutes, then increase to medium and stir, scraping the base and corners, until it is steaming and 77-80 °C, about 10 min. The crumbs thicken it early, so trust the thermometer.

steps.title: Flavour and strain
steps.text: Stir in the vanilla and black pepper, then sieve into a bowl, pressing gently on the crumbs to release the custard trapped inside.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cool over the iced water, stirring occasionally, then refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn and layer
steps.text: Chill a container while the ice cream churns, then layer the ice cream with the broken biscuits.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Cover and freeze for about 4 h until firm.

tips: Crunchy gingernut biscuits give the strongest spice flavour.
A common mistake is pressing the crumbs hard through the sieve, which makes the base gritty. Press lightly.
Serve with a drizzle of caramel sauce.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks. The biscuit pieces soften slowly over time.
